ai.definition: Skin Microbiome Engineering involves developing products that aim to rebalance the natural microflora of the skin rather than simply sterilizing it. This approach uses a combination of beneficial strains of bacteria and prebiotics to promote a healthy microbial ecosystem on the skin.
ai.howItWorks: Beneficial bacterial strains are identified, isolated, and cultured in controlled laboratory settings. These strains are then formulated into products such as serums, creams, or masks. Prebiotics, which serve as food for beneficial bacteria, are also included to support the growth of these strains on the skin. The formulations undergo extensive testing to ensure they have a positive impact on both the microbial community and overall skin health.
ai.problemSolved: Traditional skincare approaches often focus on killing harmful bacteria without considering the importance of the natural microbiome. Skin Microbiome Engineering addresses this by promoting a balanced ecosystem, which can help in managing conditions like acne, sensitivity, and barrier issues more effectively.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves careful selection and culturing of bacterial strains under sterile conditions. Prebiotics are sourced from natural or synthetic sources and combined with the bacterial cultures to create stable formulations that can be applied topically.
ai.buildProcess: Initial steps include identifying potential beneficial bacteria through genetic analysis, followed by in vitro testing for their safety and efficacy. Formulations are then developed and tested on human skin models before clinical trials.
ai.costDrivers: High costs associated with bacterial culture, rigorous testing protocols, and specialized equipment required for safe handling of live cultures.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: promising but requires further validation through clinical studies and consumer acceptance.
ai.regulation: Currently under review by regulatory bodies, requiring proof of safety and efficacy before market approval. Standards are still evolving in this field.
ai.risks: Potential for allergic reactions or unintended disruptions to the skin’s natural microbiome if not properly managed during formulation and application.
ai.profitability: Uncertain due to high initial R&D costs and need for extensive clinical validation, but could be significant once validated and adopted by consumers.
ai.futureDevelopment: Expected growth in research focusing on personalized approaches based on individual microbial profiles, as well as advancements in delivery systems to enhance product efficacy.

glossary.def: The community of microorganisms that live on or inside the human body, including bacteria, fungi, and viruses.
Non-digestible food ingredients that promote the growth of beneficial microorganisms in the gut or on skin when applied topically.

subsystems.name: Strain library and culture
subsystems.role: collects and grows skin bacteria for testing and production.

subsystems.name: Genetic engineering toolkit
subsystems.role: modifies strains to produce helpful molecules or outcompete harmful ones.

subsystems.name: Formulation and delivery
subsystems.role: keeps live cells viable in a cream, spray or patch.

subsystems.name: Skin models and assays
subsystems.role: tests how strains behave on skin without using people.

subsystems.name: Clinical and regulatory
subsystems.role: proves safety and benefit, and meets rules for live products.

buildSteps.title: Sample the skin
buildSteps.detail: Swab or scrape different body sites — oily, moist, dry — to capture the resident community.

buildSteps.title: Isolate and culture
buildSteps.detail: Grow bacteria in anaerobic chambers, since many skin microbes die in ordinary air.

buildSteps.title: Sequence and select
buildSteps.detail: Genome-sequence isolates and screen for traits like producing antimicrobials or soothing inflammation.

buildSteps.title: Engineer or adapt
buildSteps.detail: Use CRISPR or lab evolution to boost a helpful trait, or to delete a harmful one.

buildSteps.title: Formulate
buildSteps.detail: Mix the chosen strains with protectants and prebiotics, then freeze-dry or encapsulate them so they survive storage.

buildSteps.title: Test on skin models
buildSteps.detail: Apply to 3D skin models and ex vivo skin to check survival, colonisation and effects on other microbes.

buildSteps.title: Run clinical trials
buildSteps.detail: Test safety and efficacy in people with acne, eczema or sensitive skin, comparing against placebo.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture and approve
buildSteps.detail: Scale up fermentation under strict quality rules and gain regulatory approval as a live biotherapeutic product.

prerequisites.why: we know which bacteria live on skin and how the community varies between people.
many key species are hard to grow, but methods now exist.
CRISPR works in some species, but many skin microbes lack reliable tools.
we know some strains help, but the full rules of a healthy microbiome are unclear.
rules are emerging, but few products have been approved, so the path is uncertain.
keeping bacteria alive in a cosmetic or drug is hard, especially at room temperature.

pathway.milestone: research labs map which strains help or harm skin, and test them in skin models
pathway.unlocks: a list of candidate strains for specific conditions.

pathway.milestone: first controlled clinical trials of defined live strains for acne or atopic dermatitis
pathway.unlocks: evidence that rebalancing the microbiome works.

pathway.milestone: regulatory approval of the first skin live biotherapeutic product
pathway.unlocks: a new class of treatment and clearer rules for others.

pathway.milestone: engineered consortia and personalised blends based on a person's microbiome
pathway.unlocks: treatments matched to individual skin communities.
